description: 5 independently generated completeness metrics. Per Section AG: 'Do NOT collapse these into one misleading percentage.'

metrics.formula: verified complete requirements / total auditable requirements
metrics.interpretation: Only 1 of 73 prompts is verifiably complete. 61 prompts are UNVERIFIABLE (no prompt texts). 10 prompts are MISSING (artifacts never committed or never produced). 1 prompt (Prompt 73) is VERIFIED_PARTIAL (present but references missing prerequisites).
metrics.note: If we count Prompt 73 as VERIFIED_PARTIAL, the figure is 2/73 = 0.027. The conservative 0.014 counts only fully-verified-internal-implementation.

metrics.formula: requirements with sufficient evidence / total auditable requirements
metrics.numerator_detail: 1 prompt with sufficient evidence (Prompt 72 — 37 files with all JSON valid + honest-state preserved)
metrics.interpretation: Only 1 of 73 prompts has sufficient evidence. The other 72 either have no evidence (Prompts 1-61 — worklog only), missing evidence (Prompts 62-71 — artifacts never committed/produced), or partial evidence (Prompt 73 — present but references missing prerequisites).

metrics.formula: requirements with runtime evidence where applicable / runtime-applicable requirements
metrics.denominator: runtime-applicable requirements (all Pilot A execution requirements + all assurance test requirements)
metrics.numerator_detail: 0 runtime evidence — Pilot A never executed; 0 transactions; 0 KPIs; 0 replays; 0 assurance tests executed
metrics.denominator_detail: all runtime-applicable requirements (94 assurance tests + 19 BM steps × 16 scenarios + 15 KPI measurements + 15 failure scenarios + reconciliation events + finality events)
metrics.interpretation: 0% runtime completeness. No runtime evidence exists. Pilot A was never executed.

metrics.formula: requirements without confirmed regression / total tested requirements
metrics.denominator_detail: 0 tested requirements (nothing was tested — no runtime, no test execution)
metrics.interpretation: 1.000 regression-free rate is TECHNICALLY CORRECT but MISLEADING. It does NOT mean the program is healthy. It means there is nothing to regress from — the missing files were never present, so they cannot have regressed. This metric should NOT be used to claim program health.
metrics.warning: Do NOT interpret 1.000 as 'no regressions therefore healthy'. The correct interpretation is 'no prior implementation to regress from'.

metrics.formula: requirements with durable artifact/implementation evidence / total auditable requirements
metrics.numerator_detail: 2 prompts with durable committed artifacts (Prompt 72 — 37 files committed in c7dafc6; Prompt 73 — 26 files committed in c7dafc6)
metrics.interpretation: Only 2 of 73 prompts have durable artifacts committed to git. The other 71 either have no durable artifact (Prompts 1-61 — worklog Task IDs only, not full artifacts) or had artifacts that were never committed (Prompts 62-71 — developed in prior sessions but never persisted to git).
metrics.note: The 2 durable prompts (72, 73) are both from the current conversation session. The prior session work (62-71) was not persisted.

do_not_collapse_rule: Per Section AG: 'Do NOT collapse these into one misleading percentage.' The 5 metrics are reported independently. They tell different stories: implementation completeness (1.4%), evidence completeness (1.4%), runtime completeness (0%), regression-free rate (100% but misleading), durability completeness (2.7%). No single percentage captures the full picture.
